references.text: Describes the new moon sacrifices and the accompanying drink offerings that were to be brought at the beginning of each month, as mentioned in Numbers 10:10.
Refers to the day of trumpet blasts (Rosh Hashanah) when trumpets were to sound during the festival, connected to the feasts mentioned in the verse.
The regulation concerning the day of trumpet blasts in the seventh month, one of the festivals where trumpets were to be blown.
An overview of all the Lord's appointed feasts (moedim) that Israel was to celebrate, the same feasts mentioned in Numbers 10:10.
The psalm commands blowing horns at the new moon and full moon, on the festival day, as a statute for Israel.
David appointed Levites to praise, give thanks, and worship the Lord with musical instruments and trumpets before the ark of the covenant.
At the dedication of the temple, priests blew trumpets while the Levites sang and played, and the glory of the Lord filled the house.
During King Hezekiah's reforms, the burnt offering was presented with singing and trumpet sounds, as commanded by the regulation in Numbers 10:10.
At the laying of the foundation of the second temple, priests blew trumpets while they praised the Lord.
The regulation concerning the peace offerings (zivche shelamim) mentioned in Numbers 10:10 as one of the sacrifices where trumpets were to be blown.
The regulation concerning the burnt offering (olah), which is one of the sacrifices mentioned in Numbers 10:10 where trumpets were to be blown.
Paul mentions new moon festivals and feasts as shadows of what was to come, namely Christ, who fulfills these regulations.
